Stop building AI shopping assistants from scratch—Anthropic just dropped a production-ready reference blueprint for customer-facing shopping agents and human-approved merchant back-office agents. 🛒🤖

Building production-grade e-commerce AI usually means starting with a blank slate, dealing with brittle agent loops, and struggling to implement strict safety boundaries. 

The new anthropics/commerce-agents repository solves this by providing a complete, modular architecture for two distinct systems:
• Customer-Facing Shopping Assistant: Handles product search, comparisons, cart management, and policy Q&A.
• Back-Office Merchant Agent: Manages analytics, catalog updates, inventory alerts, and campaign drafting.

Key engineering features include:
🛡️ Staged Write Guardrails: Ensures strict human oversight by staging every merchant write and checkout action, rendering carts for user approval rather than executing direct charges.
⚡ Multi-Runtime Flexibility: Deploy using the exact same underlying logic across the Messages API, the Claude Agent SDK, and hosted Managed Agents via MCP servers.
🛠️ Claude Code Plugin Integration: Use native scaffolding plugins like `/scaffold-commerce-agent` and `/add-commerce-flow` to interactively build custom projects for your existing stack.
🔌 Abstract Backend Interfaces: Map your systems directly to `StorefrontBackend` and `MerchantBackend` to quickly spin up verticals in retail, travel, telecom, and entertainment.

If you are an AI engineer or full-stack developer tired of reinventing the wheel on tool-calling contracts and security fencing, check out the blueprint here:
https://github.com/anthropics/commerce-agents

What retail or travel vertical are you planning to build an agent for first? Let us know in the comments, and don't forget to star the repo! 👇

Tired of hunting down where your Mac's storage went? Finally audit and clean up the mysterious multi-gigabyte macOS System Data bucket item-by-item instead of guessing where your SSD space went.

If you are an iOS developer, full-stack engineer, or power user juggling heavy toolchains like Docker, Xcode, Node.js, Homebrew, Rust, and Go on a space-constrained SSD, your machine is constantly bleeding disk space through invisible build caches and abandoned project artifacts. Standard macOS storage settings and Finder fail to attribute these files properly.

Enter macos-sysdata: a native Swift 6 macOS menu bar utility designed to give you absolute visibility and deterministic control over your local environment.

Key Features:

Granular Auditing & Safety Badging: Classifies roughly 180 items across 18 groups with clear badges (Safe, Review, Manual) and age tracking based on last-touched or last-booted timestamps.

Transparent Root Execution: No black-box background daemons here. Root operations run as explicit, user-vetted one-off osascript prompts where you can inspect and copy the exact command before execution.

Comprehensive CLI & Scripting: Use the --json flag to print the full inventory of scanned items for automation, track historical growth, and script checks to flag bloated package manager caches before they trigger disk warnings.

Smart Shutdown Integration: Proactively terminates booted iOS simulators to drastically cut down macOS userspace teardown delays during power-off.

Reclaim dozens of gigabytes of SSD space instantly by purging orphaned Xcode DerivedData, inactive Xcode apps, and unused simulator runtimes without risking system stability.

Check out the repo, drop a star, and take back your SSD:
https://github.com/Jarvis322/macos-sysdata

Tired of manually wrestling with WARP/MASQUE configs? 🛑 

Managing Cloudflare WARP and MASQUE setups usually means dealing with tedious device registration, manual P-256 key generation, and endless YAML tinkering. 

Meet usque-custom-pro: a web-based visual management and configuration-generation tool that automates the entire pipeline. 🚀

⚡ Key Features:
• Browser-Based P-256 Key Generation & WARP Enrollment: Securely generate keys locally using WebCrypto and register via Cloudflare Pages or Workers.
• Mass Candidate Node Generation: Multiply a single credential into optimized candidate endpoints with automated latency testing and stability filtering.
• Advanced Smart Routing: Instantly output production-ready configs for Clash, Mihomo, Shadowrocket, and sing-box with pre-configured policy groups for Netflix, OpenAI, Telegram, and more.
• Local VLESS Bridge & Egress Detection: Test real-world exit IPs, geo-locations, and Cloudflare PoP routing out of the box.

Whether you are a network engineer, DevOps practitioner, or privacy-focused developer, this tool saves hours of configuration overhead and simplifies multi-client proxy management.

🔗 Check it out on GitHub:
https://github.com/KJGX66F/usque-custom-pro

Hardware vendor lock-in just took a massive hit. 💥 

What if you could run NVIDIA DLSS 5 Neural Rendering natively on AMD hardware? The open-source project danielblnc/DLSS-NR-on-AMD makes this a reality, bypassing artificial vendor restrictions to bring advanced neural rendering to competing GPUs.

For too long, cutting-edge upscaling and neural rendering tech have been trapped behind proprietary hardware walls. This project solves that by acting as a custom DirectX 12 integration layer that hooks into games utilizing AMD FSR, allowing users to run the DLSS Neural Rendering binary (nvngx_dlssnr.dll) smoothly on AMD Radeon RX 7000 and 9000 series cards.

Key Features & Engineering Highlights:
🚀 Ground-up custom neural network runtime written specifically for AMD architectures using native HIP kernels and memory layouts.
🛡️ Zero proprietary NVIDIA code at runtime—it safely hooks into the pipeline requiring only your legally obtained DLSS binary.
🎮 Seamless DirectX 12 game integration that hijacks FSR rendering pipelines to inject neural output.
🎛️ Built-in config overlay (hit the End key) for real-time tuning of tone intensity, structure, skin detail, and execution modes.

Why Graphics & Systems Engineers Need to See This:
If you work with graphics pipelines, hardware abstraction layers, or custom compute shaders, this repo is a masterclass in cross-vendor GPU programming. Dive into the code to see how native HIP kernels can bridge proprietary vendor APIs onto alternative hardware architectures, offering deep insights into memory layout mapping and heterogeneous model execution.

Check out the repository and explore the source code here:
https://github.com/danielblnc/DLSS-NR-on-AMD

👇 Drop a comment below: Are you more interested in testing this in-game or diving into the HIP kernel implementation? Star the repo if you love breaking down vendor barriers!

Tired of spinning up heavy PostgreSQL clusters and complex subgraphs just to analyze prediction markets? 

Meet PolyLedger: an open-source, resumable indexer that streams Polymarket metadata and Polygon trades directly into a local, queryable DuckDB file using standard SQL. 🚀

Analyzing decentralized prediction markets has traditionally meant dealing with the friction of scattered Polymarket CLOB metadata and raw on-chain trade data from Polygon. PolyLedger eliminates that overhead by combining Envio HyperSync with DuckDB to transform raw event logs and REST responses into a unified, high-performance local file instantly queryable with SQL. No Docker clusters required.

Here is why developers, quant researchers, and AI engineers are adding it to their stack:

🔄 Resumable & Idempotent Architecture: Commits rows and block cursors in a single transaction with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING rules, ensuring interrupted backfills resume seamlessly without data duplication.
⚡ Dual Contract Decoding: Native support for both legacy V1 and modern V2/NegRisk Polymarket CLOB exchange layouts, handling divergent event schemas and missing token IDs dynamically.
📊 Columnar Analytics with DuckDB: Stores all normalized data inside a lightweight, serverless file leveraging columnar compression for instant aggregation, complex joins, and direct Parquet exports.
🛡️ Resilient Networking: Implements token-bucket rate limiting, exponential backoff with jitter, and Pydantic-validated schema parsing to protect your ingestion pipelines against upstream API variations.

Whether you are building automated trading and market-making bots that require low-latency access to historical volume, VWAP, and order fill pricing, or exporting structured datasets to train machine learning models for election and macroeconomic event forecasting, PolyLedger gets you straight to the data.

Get started with a single Python command and skip the infrastructure headaches:
https://github.com/nahrek/polyledger
